$comment: One thing that happened, as seen by one source. This schema describes the form this project writes: proto field names, enums as names, 64-bit integers as strings, and unpopulated fields absent. It is generated from proto/audit/v1/record.proto together with that file's comments, and the proto itself is archived beside it.

Actor.description: Actor is who acted. `kind` selects a registered actor kind, which declares the schema of `attributes` and the identity treatment.

attributes.description: Kind-specific attributes, validated against the kind's schema.

credential_hash.description: SHA-256 of the credential used, base64, so a token can be found without ever storing it.

session_id.description: Session identifier, if any. Audit only; hashed by the writer when the actor kind says so.

Capture.description: Capture is the level-gated request and response snapshot.

request.description: An extension slot. Its shape is the JSON Schema the catalogue registers for it; numbers in it must be integers a float64 holds exactly.

response.description: An extension slot. Its shape is the JSON Schema the catalogue registers for it; numbers in it must be integers a float64 holds exactly.

truncated.description: True when any capped field was truncated, in the documented order.

additionalProperties.description: An extension slot. Its shape is the JSON Schema the catalogue registers for it; numbers in it must be integers a float64 holds exactly.

areas.description: Extension slots keyed by area ("http", "rpc", "k8s", "github"), each validated against the area's registered schema.

client_addresses.description: Client address chain, nearest last, as the trusted hop count leaves it.

Meter.description: Meter is the usage measurement of a billable action or a periodic gauge sample. Counts are events; gauges are absolute samples, never deltas.

dimensions.description: Flat primitives only, validated against the meter's dimensions schema.

Observer.description: Observer is the reporting component, stamped by the writer.

id.description: Verified workload identity of the publisher.

instance.description: Instance name (pod name), the producer of `sequence`.

Outcome.description: Outcome is how the action ended, with a source-specific code.

reason.description: Human-readable reason, bounded, never containing secrets.

Party.description: Party is a subject: a kind from the registry and its identifier. The identifier is a stable id or a keyed pseudonym; never a name or e-mail.

Target.description: Target is what the action was done to. `type` selects a registered target type, which declares the schema of `attributes` and whether `name` may be carried.

attributes.description: An extension slot. Its shape is the JSON Schema the catalogue registers for it; numbers in it must be integers a float64 holds exactly.

name.description: Display name, allowed only where the target type's registration says the target is not a person.

description: Record is one thing that happened, as seen by one source.  Which copies carry a given core field is decided by the profile a copy is written under, through the presets it is composed from (docs/concepts.md); the record itself does not say. An extension property, by contrast, carries its class as an annotation on its schema.

action.description: What happened, "resource.verb" under the source's namespace, from the catalogue.

actor.description: Who did it. Identity treatment is decided by the actor kind's registration.

attributes.description: Bounded free-form attributes for what has no schema yet. Bounds are enforced by the emitter library (key count, key and value length).

capture.description: Request and response capture, level-gated and size-capped.

catalogue_version.description: Version of the source's catalogue that describes this action and its extension slots. Resolved by the writer; unknown versions dead-letter, never drop.

data.description: Extension slot keyed by `action`; validated against the schema the catalogue registers for it. Class per property by annotation.

id.description: Identity of the record. UUIDv7 minted by the emitter; the idempotency key at every hop.

observer.description: Who reported the record. Stamped by the writer from the publisher's verified workload identity; an emitter cannot set it.

occurred_at.description: When the thing happened, from the emitter's synchronised clock.

operation.description: Coarse classification of the action, orthogonal to `action`.

origin_hash.description: Set by the writer on every profile copy: SHA-256 of the canonical wide record before the split, so copies are provably the same original.

previous_attributes.description: On update actions only: the prior values of changed attributes, whole arrays when any element changed.

profile.description: Set by the writer on a profile copy: which profile this copy is. Absent on the wire from an emitter.

recorded_at.description: When the split writer accepted the record. Set by the writer, never by the emitter. Drives the tail cursor and lateness alerts.

schema_version.description: Core schema version, "major.minor". Equal-on-major, greater-or-equal- on-minor is the compatibility contract.

sequence.description: Sequence per producer instance, monotonic, for gap detection. The producer name is `observer.instance`.

source.description: The system the event is about ("keycloak", "wallet", "roster"). Also the namespace prefix of `action`.

subject.description: Whom it concerns, when that is not the actor. Identity treatment is decided by the subject kind's registration.

tenant_id.description: The customer the record belongs to. A legal entity, never a person. Stays in clear in every profile. A reserved value names the platform itself for events with no tenant.

unmapped.description: Fields a source could not map onto the record. Kept so nothing is silently lost; promoted to `data` or the core when they recur.

title: Audit record 1.0
